findings.title: `import()` calls run eagerly at module load, so no app is actually lazy-loaded
findings.body:
Each property of the `appStore` object literal is initialised with `import("./x")`. That call starts the import as soon as `index.ts` is evaluated. Importing `@calcom/app-store` therefore still loads all ~28 app packages up front, which defeats the PR's goal of async/lazy imports.

The cost is that every caller now pays for an `await` and has an async signature, with no reduction in load cost.

There is a second problem: if any single app module fails to load, its promise rejects whether or not anyone ever reads that key. Nothing handles that rejection, so it surfaces as an unhandled promise rejection at startup.

Fix: store thunks instead, e.g. `applecalendar: () => import("./applecalendar")`, and call them on demand in `getCalendar`, `getVideoAdapters` and the payment helpers.

findings.title: `forEach(async ...)` escapes the surrounding try/catch, causing unhandled rejections
findings.body:
The callback is now `async` and awaits `getCalendar`. The returned promises are discarded by `forEach`.

Any error from `getCalendar` (app import failure, a `CalendarService` constructor throwing) or from `deleteEvent`/`deleteMeeting` becomes a rejected promise. The surrounding try/catch, which is meant to log these errors, never sees it.

Previously a synchronous `getCalendar` error was caught there. Now it is an unhandled rejection, which can terminate the Node process under default settings. The deletions are also not awaited before the reschedule email is sent.

Fix: use `await Promise.allSettled(bookingRefsFiltered.map(async ...))` or a `for...of` loop.

findings.title: `forEach(async ...)` escapes try/catch, causing unhandled rejections
findings.body:
This is the same problem as in `vital/lib/reschedule.ts`.

The async `forEach` callback's promises are dropped. Failures in `getCalendar`, `deleteEvent` or `deleteMeeting` are no longer caught by the enclosing try/catch and become unhandled promise rejections. The deletes are also not awaited before the reschedule email is sent.

Fix: replace with `Promise.allSettled` over `map`, or with a `for...of` loop.

findings.title: `requestReschedule` fires async calendar/video deletes without awaiting or handling errors
findings.body:
`bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async ...)` now awaits `getCalendar` inside each callback. The resulting promises are discarded.

Any rejection from `getCalendar`, `deleteEvent` or `deleteMeeting` is unhandled, with a risk of process crash on Node 15+. The mutation also returns, and sends emails and webhooks, before the external events are actually removed.

Fix: collect the promises with `map` and `await Promise.allSettled(...)`.
